name: Roast Chicken Leg Quarters
why: The most forgiving meat in the kitchen. Leg meat has fat running through it, so unlike breast it does not dry out if you leave it in too long.

ingredients.display: The Keg BBQ chicken seasoning, or paprika + garlic powder

steps.text: THE NIGHT BEFORE: move the quarters from the freezer to the fridge on a plate.
steps.look: They need roughly 12 hours to thaw. A plate underneath catches the liquid that comes out, which you do not want running around a fridge shelf.
steps.warn: Never thaw meat on the counter. The outside sits in the bacterial danger zone for hours while the middle is still frozen.

steps.text: Oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a tray with parchment.
steps.look: Hotter than most roasting. Chicken skin needs real heat to render its fat and crisp. At 350 it goes pale and rubbery instead.

steps.text: Pat every quarter completely dry with paper towel, all over, especially the skin.
steps.look: Do not rush this. Wet skin steams and stays flabby. Dry skin crisps. This is the single step that decides whether the skin is good.

steps.text: Rub 1 tbsp of oil over them, then season with 1 tsp kosher salt, 2 tsp of seasoning and 1/2 tsp black pepper, top and bottom.
steps.look: Get some under the skin if it lifts easily at the edge. Skin blocks seasoning from reaching the meat, so anything sitting on top only flavours the skin itself.

steps.text: Skin side up on the tray, spaced apart. Roast 40 to 45 minutes.
steps.look: Space matters: quarters touching each other steam where they touch. Do not turn them, do not open the oven for the first 30 minutes.Done at 175°F in the thickest part of the thigh, not touching bone. Dark meat wants 175, higher than the 165 for breast, because the connective tissue in a leg needs the extra heat to soften.
steps.warn: If the skin is browning too fast at 30 minutes, that is fine, keep going. Dark skin on a leg quarter is flavour, not burning. Trust the thermometer over the colour.

steps.look: Roughly 38 g of protein per quarter: ~170 g across 4.5 quarters in a 1.5 kg pack, bone-in weight, so the edible meat is less than the pack weight suggests.Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days. Pull the meat off the bones before refrigerating, it takes half the space and you will actually use it.
